title: Image of a Picard immersion equals the trivial-fibre locus in a family with a section
statement: Let f:P→S be a morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-over-base] with a section σ:S→P [def-pc-section], and let L be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] on P. Let j:T→S be an immersion. Suppose that for every B→S the morphism factors through j if and only if the restriction of L to P×_S B [def-pc-fibre-product] is the pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] of a finite locally free module on B. Then the set-theoretic image of j equals the set of s∈S for which the restriction of L to P_s=P×_S Spec κ(s) [def-weil-residue-field] is trivial. No properness, flatness or connectedness assumption is needed in this assertion.

proof.text: For s in the image of j, the canonical map g:Spec κ(s)→S lifts through j. Indeed, an immersion is surjective on stalks, hence its residue-field maps are field isomorphisms. For a point t with j(t)=s, compose Spec of the inverse residue-field map with the canonical residue-field morphism of t. This is the existing proved Scheme.exists_comp_eq_of_mem_range, applied to g; the image of its closed point is s.

Evaluate the assumed universal factorization property at g. It supplies a finite locally free module N on Spec κ(s) with q*L≅p*N, where q and p are the two fibre projections. The tensorPullback and source-library pullback functors are naturally isomorphic by uniqueness of left adjoints to pushforward, so transport the supplied isomorphism to ordinary module pullbacks.

Base change the section σ to r:Spec κ(s)→P_s. Pulling the isomorphism back along r gives (r≫q)*L≅N, since r≫p=id. Pullback preserves invertibility, so N is invertible. An invertible module on Spec of a field is trivial: apply the existing IsInvertible.nonempty_iso_unit at its unique point. Pulling this trivialization back along p trivializes q*L.

Conversely, if q*L is trivial, use N=O in the universal property. The structure module is finite locally free. The unit pullback isomorphism and the canonical comparison of the two pullback functors supply its required isomorphism. The resulting factorization g=h≫j, evaluated at the closed point of Spec κ(s), places s in the image of j. These implications give equality of the two sets.
